  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Quickstart: Building a hyperdesign and running KEMA/GPA}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

This short vignette shows how to construct a minimal `hyperdesign` from
plain matrices and label vectors using `as_hyperdesign()`, then run
KEMA and Generalized Procrustes (GPA) via `align_many()` with the
native multi-view adapters.

```r
library(manifoldalign)
set.seed(1)

# Two domains with simple class labels
X1 <- matrix(rnorm(200), 100, 2)
X2 <- matrix(rnorm(200), 100, 2)
y1 <- sample(c("A","B"), 100, TRUE)
y2 <- sample(c("A","B"), 100, TRUE)

# Build a minimal hyperdesign object (no multidesign dependency needed)
hd <- as_hyperdesign(list(X1, X2), labels = list(y1, y2), label_name = "label",
                     domain_names = c("d1","d2"))

# KEMA (native multi-view)
# Note: pass y as a bare symbol referring to the label column in each domain
# (eval=FALSE to keep vignette fast)
# res_kema <- align_many(hd, kema_aligner(), y = label, ncomp = 2)

# GPA (Generalized Procrustes; native multi-view)
# Here the label is interpreted as a task identifier per sample/column after
# appropriate preprocessing inside GPA. For simple matrices, this quickstart
# demonstrates the routing only. See ?generalized_procrustes for details.
# res_gpa <- align_many(hd, gpa_aligner(), y = label, max_iter = 50)

# For pairwise methods (e.g., PARROT or GRASP), use align_many() the same way,
# and the driver will perform synchronization to a consensus.
```

Tip: For larger N, configure `graph="auto"` and `sync` options in
`align_many()` to choose spectral permutation consensus, GL least-squares,
or orthogonal rotation synchronization.
